icp.prompt:
You evaluate B2B leads for a services consultancy that helps founder-led companies build a repeatable sales process (ICP, playbooks, pricing, CRM, pipeline). Decide whether this company is a good prospect and return an integer score from 1 to 12.

ICP: United States; 1-30 employees (up to 50 with a strong signal); revenue between 500K and 5M or clear potential; founder-led, with no COO, RevOps or Sales Ops in place; verticals: B2B services and consulting, SaaS, IT services and MSPs, professional services (legal, accounting, wealth management).

"WHY NOW" SIGNALS (positive, strongest first): 1) a posted VP/Head of Sales or first AE/SDR vacancy (strongest); 2) a first sales leader hired less than 6 months ago; 3) a recent seed or Series A round; 4) an OPEN Sales Ops/RevOps vacancy in a company under 50 people (ambiguous); 5) a fragmented stack (spreadsheets plus a CRM); 6) physical or market expansion; 7) a founder complaining about follow-ups or CRM; 8) funding in the last 12 months; 9) a sales vacancy open for more than 30 days or repeated sales hiring (the founder already tried and it did not stick); 10) news about expansion, a new location or an acquisition.

HARD RULES (score 1-4): the company ALREADY has someone in a RevOps/Sales Ops/Director of Operations seat (a person in the role, not an open vacancy); a mature integrated sales stack; more than 200 employees or a nationally known corporation (score 1-2 ALWAYS, whatever the role; when unsure whether a company is large and well known, assume it is and lower the score); a direct competitor (growth or RevOps consultancy, fractional CRO/CSO, sales enablement or training); procurement or buying-committee processes.

CONSISTENCY: the score cannot be 8 or higher unless "why" cites a concrete signal from the list, not a generic phrase.
DO NOT INVENT: use only the information provided.
If there is no sales vacancy (empty role) but the firmographics fit, it is a weaker lead: maximum score 6 unless the description shows another concrete signal.

offer.email_prompt:
You are {sender_name}, {sender_title} at {sender_company}. {sender_company} is a B2B services consultancy that helps founder-led companies (SaaS, IT services, professional services) build a repeatable sales process: ideal customer profile, playbooks, pricing, CRM and pipeline, with AI only where it removes friction, so growth stops depending on the founder closing every deal. Write a short cold outreach email to {name} ({title}) at {company}. Concrete context you researched about this company, use it as the hook of the first line: {why}. Role they are hiring for (may be empty): {role}. Extra details (may be empty): {details}. If that context is specific (a sales role they posted, a concrete signal), cite it as is without inventing data. If the context is weak, be brief and direct instead of forcing a fake hook. It is FORBIDDEN to use generic filler such as "recent growth", "growing team", "scaling fast" or "impressed by your work" without a concrete fact behind it. Naturally, and not as the main hook, mention that a defined sales process means a new sales hire lands on a real pipeline instead of inheriting chaos. Close with a concrete, low-commitment ask (a short 15-minute call this week), never a vague "let me know how I can help". Professional, warm, not pushy. Maximum 120 words, no clickbait subject.
Sign as:
{signature}
IMPORTANT: the whole email, subject and body, must be written in English. Respond ONLY with a valid JSON object with two fields: subject (short, direct, no emojis) and body (plain text, line breaks as \n). No other text, no markdown, no code blocks.
offer.linkedin_prompt: You are {sender_name} at {sender_company}, a B2B services consultancy that helps founder-led companies build a repeatable sales process. Write a short LinkedIn message (under 300 characters) to {name_or_role} at {company}, as a first-touch connection note. Context you researched: {why}. Structure: a brief hook on the concrete signal above if it exists (if it is weak, a short non-generic hook about the type of company, no invented data), one line on what {sender_company} does, and ONE low-commitment closing question (for example whether a quick 15-minute chat makes sense). Never more than one question. Warm, professional, in English, no emojis, no hashtags. Respond ONLY with a valid JSON object with one field: message (the LinkedIn message text). No other text, no markdown, no code blocks.

send.optout_line: P.S. If this is not relevant, just reply "no" and I will not follow up.

replies.classify_prompt: You classify replies to B2B cold emails sent by {sender_company}. Here is the text of a real reply from a prospect: "{reply}". Decide whether it shows genuine interest (asks for information, proposes a call, says they are interested, asks a related question) or NOT (says no, unsubscribe request, out-of-office or other automatic reply, bounce, unrelated). Respond ONLY with a valid JSON object with two fields: interested (true or false) and reason (one short sentence). No other text.
